Consent Calendar

1.-Amendments to Berkeley Municipal Code (BMC) Section 23.304.100 (Site Features in Residential Districts) to require undergrounding of electrical transformers on private land
From: City Manager
Recommendation: Adopt second reading of Ordinance No. 8,035-N.S. amending Berkeley Municipal Code (BMC) Section 23.304.100 (Site Features in Residential Districts) to prohibit the above-ground installation of electrical transformers serving new residential, commercial, and mixed-use projects grade on private property, consistent with the Planning Commission’s recommendation.
First Reading Vote: Ayes – Kesarwani, Tregub, O’Keefe, Blackaby, Lunaparra, Humbert, Ishii; Noes – None; Abstain – None; Absent – Taplin, Bartlett.
Financial Implications: See report
Contact: Jordan Klein, Planning and Development, (510) 981-7400

30.-Ashby BART East Lot Developer Selection for Exclusive Negotiation and Reservation of Predevelopment Funding
From: City Manager
Recommendation: Adopt two Resolutions that enable the City to move forward into negotiation and predevelopment with a selected development team for the Ashby East Lot Transit Oriented Development (TOD) project, located at the intersection of Woolsey St. and Tremont St., directly east of the Ed Roberts Campus, by: 
1. Authorizing the City Manager or designee to negotiate and enter into an Exclusive Negotiating Rights Agreement (ENRA) and any required amendments with Satellite Affordable Housing Associates (SAHA), Habitat for Humanity East Bay/Silicon Valley, and Deborah D. Matthews Consulting (collectively, “the SAHA Team”). 
2. Authorizing the City Manager or designee to negotiate and enter into an ENRA and any required amendments with the alternative developer, Related California and the Kelsey (collectively, “the Related Team”), in the event that the ENRA with the SAHA Team is terminated or if the City does not enter into a ENRA with the SAHA Team. 3. Approving the reservation of $1 million of Affordable Housing Mitigation Fees (Fund 120) to the SAHA Team or their affiliate(s) to support master planning and predevelopment activities related to the development of affordable housing at the Ashby East Lot BART site. 4. Affirming that the City's Housing Trust Fund Guidelines will apply to the use of funds to support master planning and predevelopment activities related to the development of affordable housing at the Ashby East Lot BART site. 5. Authorizing the City Manager or designee to execute all original or amended documents or agreements in accordance with the intent of this Resolution. 
Financial Implications: See report
Contact: Scott Gilman, Health, Housing, and Community Services, (510) 981-5100
